name: When should finish selections be made in preconstruction?

mainEntity.name: How early do I need to choose materials, fixtures, and finishes?
mainEntity.text: How early do I need to choose materials, fixtures, and finishes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Finish selections should be made early because they affect both cost and schedule. The sooner the team knows what materials, fixtures, and appliances you want, the more accurate the budget will be. Early selections also help identify long-lead items that may need to be ordered before construction starts. If selections are delayed, the builder must use allowances or assumptions, which can make the budget less reliable. That is not necessarily a problem, but it does create more uncertainty. The more custom and high-end the project, the more important early selections become. A practical approach is to prioritize the items that influence pricing the most: cabinetry, tile, flooring, plumbing fixtures, lighting, windows, and appliances. Those categories often drive both cost and lead time. Decorative items can sometimes wait longer, but major selections should not. For Los Angeles luxury homes, early finish decisions are part of good preconstruction discipline. They help the team lock in pricing, coordinate procurement, and reduce delays. Ask your builder which selections need to be finalized before permit submission and which can wait. That keeps the project moving and avoids surprises once construction starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Finish selections should be made as early as possible, ideally during preconstruction or before pricing is finalized. Early choices improve budget accuracy and help order long-lead items on time. Delayed selections often create allowances, pricing uncertainty, and schedule impacts once construction begins.
